articles.title: Nvidia says it's building an ecosystem that can't fail
articles.summary: The concern around Nvidia's latest turn as the central bank of AI is that alongside building coveted products, it's wielding financial power to rouse the cus...
articles.body:
Don't call it circular financing. Nvidia doesn't see its efforts to prop up upstarts and bolster key AI players as questionable financial engineering.

Yes, it's true that the beneficiaries of Nvidia's muscular backstops and investments are also its customers. But Nvidia doesn't see the scale of its support as something worthy of suspicion. That's because, the company says, it's building an ecosystem with too many scenarios for Nvidia to win.

A key question from critics of Nvidia concerns the demand for AI components, tools, and infrastructure: Would the growth around AI and the confident projections of future success be attainable without Nvidia's heavy hand ?

CFO Colette Kress addressed the criticism head-on during the company's Q2 earnings call on Wednesday.

"We know some will call this circular financing. We see it differently. We are going through a major computing platform shift, the creation of one of the most important technologies in human history, and these are once-in-a-generation companies. Their technology leadership is proven, and their customer traction and usage are skyrocketing."

From Nvidia's perspective, the success of AI labs is independent of its partnerships. But why miss out on opportunities for more growth , greater revenue diversity, and the encouragement of other firms and would-be customers to put skin in the game?

And after all, Nvidia expects some of the frontier AI labs it's doing business with to become the largest tech companies in history (apologies to the Magnificent Seven).

But what's the difference between Nvidia's vision of a thriving AI ecosystem ( with it at the financial and technological center ) and a bullheaded belief that Nvidia is building a business environment that can't fail?

Nvidia has left some room for doubt. But not much.

"We believe these investments, measured against the strength of their demand, the business they create for us, the ecosystem they build on Nvidia's platform, and the equity returns on our invested capital will be excellent, and our risk is limited," Kress said on the call.

Demand from AI labs receiving some form of financial support from Nvidia will account for about a quarter of the company's business next year, Kress said.

A bullish reading on all of this is that Nvidia's true exposure to the debt they are helping finance for the AI build-out is narrow; that expanding its client base beyond the tech giants is a savvy bet-making; and that, in a rising-AI-tide that lifts all boats, Nvidia will be the one outfitting the vessels and helping to construct new ones.

articles.title: Bank of America doubles down on Nvidia stock
articles.summary: Bank of America’s analysis had more to do with what the company is hiding in its balance sheet than what it reported for Q2 2027.
articles.body:
Nvidia reported earnings on Aug. 26. Wall Street expected it to beat. Bank of America was not particularly interested in that part of the story.

The firm's note, published ahead of the report, was really about one thing: whether the market had correctly priced the scale of what Nvidia has been doing with its balance sheet.

The answer, according to Bank of America, was no. The results Nvidia delivered made that argument harder to dismiss.

Bank of America's Buy rating and $350 Nvidia price target

In a note shared with TheStreet on Aug. 25, analyst Vivek Arya reiterated a Buy rating and a $350 price target on Nvidia, implying roughly 64% upside from where the stock was trading that day.

The note's title says everything about where the firm directed investor attention: "Balance sheet disclosures could speak louder than EPS beat."

Nvidia delivered revenue of $96.2 billion for the second fiscal quarter, up 106% year over year and well above consensus expectations of roughly $92 billion, according to Nvidia's official earnings release . Data center revenue came in at $89 billion, up 117% year over year. Gross margin held at 75%.

"AI has reached its inflection point. It's doing useful work. Its tokens are productive and profitable. Now, compute is revenue," Jensen Huang said on the earnings call. "And demand is accelerating."

Nvidia also returned roughly $26 billion to shareholders in the quarter through buybacks and dividends, with approximately $99 billion remaining under its buyback authorization.

What the market had not priced properly, Bank of America argued, was the scale of what Nvidia had committed financially to keep the AI ecosystem running.

Nvidia's $300 billion AI capital commitments and balance sheet risk

Nvidia is no longer just selling chips. It is increasingly financing the companies that buy them.

Bank of America estimated total capital commitments of approximately $300 billion, split between roughly $70 billion in direct equity investments and roughly $230 billion in residual value guarantees and backstops.

The equity side covers much of the AI supply chain, according to CNBC . The largest single check was $30 billion for OpenAI. Beyond that, Nvidia has invested in Anthropic, Safe Superintelligence, Intel, CoreWeave, Nebius, Lumentum, Coherent, Marvell, Synopsys, Nokia, Corning, and others.

articles.title: India’s first bullet train project began with a Rs 1.1 lakh crore estimate, cost has now nearly doubled to Rs 2.1 lakh crore; indigenously made high-speed train to start running from August 2027
articles.summary: India Business News: India’s first bullet train project has seen its cost escalate to nearly double of the original estimate in a span of nine years. Prime Minister Narend.
articles.body: India’s first bullet train project has seen its cost escalate to nearly double of the original estimate in a span of nine years. Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone for the first high-speed rail project of Indian Railways in September 2017, and after missed deadlines due to the pandemic, the first bullet train is expected to be operational from the later half of 2027.But these nine years have led to the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail project’s cost rising sharply, and the Ministry of Railways is now looking at approvals for the revised cost.The bullet train project is also becoming a platform for India's own high-speed rail ambitions. BEML and ICF are developing India's first indigenous high-speed trainset, with the first expected to roll out in 2027. The trains are being designed for operating speeds of around 250 kmph, with a design speed of 280 kmph.The government is already looking beyond the first corridor, with seven additional high-speed rail routes under consideration, including Bengaluru-Chennai, Bengaluru-Hyderabad and Bengaluru-Pune-Mumbai.Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train: Revised cost nearly double of originalThe estimated cost of the Ahmedabad-Mumbai bullet train project has been raised to around Rs 2.1 lakh crore, almost twice the original estimate of approximately Rs 1.1 lakh crore. A proposal seeking approval for the revised cost of the 508-km high-speed rail corridor was placed before the Cabinet on Tuesday, this TOI report said.Sources quoted in the report said the railway ministry has attributed the cost increase mainly to the prolonged land acquisition process in Maharashtra and delays in receiving the train sets from Japan.The full bullet train project between Mumbai and Ahmedabad is now expected to be completed in 2030, while the first section of the corridor is scheduled to become operational in August 2027, likely between Surat and Bilimora. Most of the additional funding is likely to come through budgetary support, the sources said.So far, the project’s Rs 1.1 lakh crore funding has come from the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) and budgetary allocations.Sources said Railways has also indicated that the high-speed trains will be manufactured in India, with each train expected to cost around Rs 390 crore to Rs 400 crore. There was no official briefing on the decisions taken at the Cabinet meeting chaired by PM Narendra Modi.In January, railway board chairperson Satish Kumar had said the project cost had risen by around 83% to Rs 1.98 lakh crore. The project has experienced both time and cost overruns due to several factors, including delays in land acquisition, statutory clearances and finalisation of the trains.Bullet train project construction progressesViaducts are taking shape across Gujarat and Maharashtra, and the tunnel construction is progressing near Mumbai and stations are being built.The corridor is being developed by National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) with Japanese technical and financial assistance and will use Shinkansen technology. It will have 12 stations and trains capable of speeds up to 320 kmph.A major engineering challenge is the 7-km undersea tunnel near Thane Creek. The project also includes seven mountain tunnels and 17 river bridges. The corridor uses Japan's J-Slab ballastless track system, being deployed in India for the first time, along with specialised track-laying machinery and training for Indian engineers and technicians.Meanwhile the Integral Coach Factory (ICF), Chennai, has awarded BEML Limited a Rs 866.87 crore contract to design and manufacture two prototype bullet train sets capable of 280 kmph.Under the contract, BEML will be responsible for the design, manufacturing and commissioning of two eight-coach high-speed trainsets. The trains are scheduled to be rolled out in 2027, while sources told TOI that the designs are currently being finalised.The bullet trains will feature fully air-conditioned chair cars equipped with world-class passenger amenities. They will also have advanced onboard infotainment systems, reclining and rotatable seats and dedicated facilities for divyangjans.BEML has established a dedicated ‘Aditya’ High-Speed Rail Complex in Bengaluru for the production of the bullet trains.The high-speed trainsets, which carry the codename B-28, will be manufactured using advanced precision-driven technologies. Bullet trains operating in countries such as Japan and across Europe are generally designed to operate in cold climates. For the Indian trains, however, conditions involving heat and dust will be taken into consideration during manufacturing.For the time being, Indian Railways plans to manufacture the bullet trains using stainless steel. Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has already announced that the next generation of bullet trains will be designed to operate at speeds of 350 kmph.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.summary: Today, Thursday, August 27, 2026, the 30-year fixed-rate purchase loan rose 4 basis points to 6.57%; the 15-year fixed purchase loan increased by 3 basis poi...
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

Mortgage held steady near 6.7% again this week as oil prices fluctuated and new data showed inflation remained elevated in July.

The average 30-year mortgage rate was 6.66% through Wednesday, according to Freddie Mac data, essentially unchanged from 6.65% a week earlier.

Mortgage rates have been hovering around 6.7% for a month straight amid ongoing investor fears about the Iran War's effect on oil prices and broader inflation. On Wednesday, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation metric showed that inflation remained sticky in July, with prices excluding the volatile food and energy categories up 3.3% from a year ago.

"Mortgage rates have climbed for much of the year, driven largely by the Iran conflict's effect on oil prices, which has kept inflation expectations, and by extension mortgage rates, elevated," Realtor.com senior economist Hannah Jones said in a statement.

Here are the current purchase mortgage rates for today, Thursday, August 27, 2026 , according to the latest Zillow data:

Remember, these are the national averages and rounded to the nearest hundredth.

Here are the current refinance mortgage rates for today, Thursday, August 27, 2026 , according to the latest Zillow data:

As with mortgage rates for purchase, these are national averages that we've rounded to the nearest hundredth. Refinance rates can be higher than purchase mortgage rates, but that isn't always the case.

Use the mortgage calculator below to see how various mortgage rates will impact your monthly payments.

You can bookmark the Yahoo Finance mortgage payment calculator and keep it handy for future use, as you shop for homes and lenders. Be sure to use the dropdown to include private mortgage insurance costs and HOA dues if they apply to you. These monthly expenses, along with your mortgage principal and interest rate, will give you a realistic idea of what your monthly payment could be.

A mortgage interest rate is the fee charged by a lender for borrowing money, expressed as a percentage. There are two basic types of mortgage rates: fixed and adjustable rates.

A fixed-rate mortgage locks in your rate for the entire life of your loan. For example, if you get a 30-year mortgage with a 6% interest rate, your rate will remain at 6% for the entire 30 years. (Unless you refinance or sell the home.)

An adjustable-rate mortgage keeps your rate the same for the first few years, then changes it periodically. Let's say you get a 5/1 ARM with an introductory rate of 6%. Your rate would be 6% for the first five years, and then the rate would increase or decrease once per year for the last 25 years of your term. Whether your rate goes up or down depends on several factors, such as the economy and the U.S. housing market.

At the beginning of your mortgage term, most of your monthly payment goes toward interest. As time passes, less of your payment goes toward interest, and more goes toward the mortgage principal or the amount you originally borrowed.

Two categories determine mortgage rates : those you can control and those you cannot.

What factors can you control? First, you can compare the best mortgage lenders to find the one that gives you the lowest rate and fees.

Second, lenders typically extend lower rates to people with higher credit scores, lower debt-to-income (DTI) ratios , and considerable down payments. If you can save more or pay down debt before securing a mortgage, a lender will probably give you a better interest rate.

What factors can you not control? In short, the economy.

The list of ways the economy impacts mortgage rates is long, but here are the basic details. If the economy — for example, employment rates — is struggling, mortgage rates decrease to encourage borrowing, which helps boost the economy. If the economy is strong, mortgage rates go up to temper spending.

With all other factors being equal, mortgage refinance rates are typically slightly higher than purchase rates. So don't be surprised if your refinance rate is higher than you may have expected.

30-year vs. 15-year fixed mortgage rates

Two of the most common mortgage terms are 30-year and 15-year fixed-rate mortgages . Both lock in your rate for the entire loan term.

A 30-year mortgage is popular because it has relatively low monthly payments. But it comes with a higher interest rate than shorter terms, and because you're accumulating interest for three decades, you'll pay a lot of interest in the long run.

A 15-year mortgage can be a good choice because it has a lower rate than you'll get with longer terms, so you'll pay less in interest over the years. You'll also pay off your mortgage much faster. But your monthly payments will be higher because you're paying off the same loan amount in half the time.

Basically, 30-year mortgages are more affordable from month to month, while 15-year mortgages are cheaper in the long run.

What bank is offering the lowest mortgage rates?

According to Yahoo Finance's weekly survey of lenders with the lowest rates , some of the banks with the lowest median mortgage rates are Flagstar , Chase , and Citibank . However, it's a good idea to shop around for the best rate, not just with banks, but also with credit unions and companies specializing in mortgage lending.

articles.title: Welcome to the ‘upper-middle-class trap’: why $300,000 a year doesn’t feel like winning anymore
articles.summary: Investopedia put a $5 million price tag on the American Dream, but Nick Maggiulli says six-figure earners are more financially fragile than they look.
articles.body:
Over the last year, Nick Maggiulli has come to what he calls an unsettling realization: The upper-middle class is caught in a trap, and many of them don't even realize it.

The chief operating officer of Ritholtz Wealth Management has spent the better part of a year building the case in pieces on his blog, Of Dollars and Data —first arguing private school isn't worth the cost despite its price tag, then that premium travel experiences have grown crowded while remaining expensive in "The Death of the Amex Lounge." He previously talked to Fortune about his book, The Wealth Ladder , and his growing belief "something weird's going on" with the upper-middle class in the U.S. economy.

In an April essay, he pulled the threads together and gave the phenomenon a name: the "upper-middle-class trap," in which people earning roughly $200,000 to $400,000 a year are working more and relaxing less to buy products and services of declining quality.

His evidence includes new single-family homes shrinking in average size by 12% between 2014 and 2024, even as the price per square foot surged 74%, according to LendingTree data . A home near a public elementary school with a top GreatSchools rating costs 78.6% more than a comparable home in the surrounding county. Homebuyers who win bidding wars end up worse off: One study found their purchases produced 6.9% lower annualized returns than homes bought without competition. In higher education, the number of college applicants has jumped 78% since 2015 even as acceptance rates at elite schools have collapsed, driving tuition and private-school costs up roughly twice as fast as overall inflation.

The mechanism Maggiulli describes is a "financial arms race": Every individual decision is rational, but collectively the competition for the same scarce positional goods lowers everyone's quality of life while draining their bank accounts.

One accelerant, he argues, is nearly impossible to opt out of. Citing Brookings Institution data from November 2025, he notes AI usage rises from 9% among earners below $30,000 to 34% among those earning $100,000 or more. High earners, worried AI threatens their careers, are forced to adopt it just to defend their position—a " Red Queen " dynamic in which everyone runs faster just to stay in place.

"If AI doubled everyone's productivity overnight," he writes, "suddenly someone with half your skill would be able to compete with you just by using AI."

His prescribed exit is blunt: Stop competing for positional goods that don't materially improve your life. Send your kids to good public schools, fly economy, buy a smaller, affordable house. His test for any big purchase: "Am I buying this to improve my quality of life, or merely because other people are buying it?"

articles.title: GLP-1 users cut portions, but biscuits and sweets stay in the basket: Study
articles.summary: India Business News: Study of GLP-1 users in Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru finds smaller portions and appetite drops, but households still buy biscuits, sweets and fried snacks.
articles.body: Bengaluru: GLP-1 users surveyed across three Indian metros reported sharply reducing their food intake after starting the medication. But biscuits, sweets and fried snacks have not disappeared from their family grocery baskets, according to a study by International Flavors & Fragrances (IFF).Participants said they had cut their intake from three or four chapatis to one or two, and from five or six idlis to two. Rice portions fell from about two-and-a-half bowls to half a bowl. Overall, 65% said their appetite had reduced significantly.The change in individual eating habits, however, was not fully reflected in household purchases. About 78% said their households continued to buy biscuits, while 71% still purchased packaged sweets. The same proportion continued buying full-fat dairy products, and 63% bought fried snacks.The findings point to the influence of shared meals and family preferences. While a person taking GLP-1 medication may eat considerably less, other members of the household may continue consuming the same products.GLP-1 medicines are used for diabetes and weight management and can reduce appetite and food intake. IFF’s study covered more than 100 users across Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru and combined in-home interviews, quantitative research, sensory testing and product tasting, the company said.The impact extended beyond portion sizes. About 90% of respondents said food tasted or felt different after they started taking the medication. Half said they preferred soft, easy-to-digest textures, while 69% wanted flavours to be balanced rather than overpowering.Eating less also affected social occasions. About 64% said they experienced discomfort while eating with others at least sometimes, including situations where they wanted to participate in a meal but were unable to eat as much as those around them.Shopping habits, meanwhile, appeared to become more deliberate. About 74% said they read food labels more carefully than before starting GLP-1 medication. Yet only 47% said they trusted claims displayed on the front of food packs.Hydration also gained importance, with nearly three-fourths treating staying hydrated as a daily goal. About 69% said they chose coconut water.IFF, which supplies flavours and food ingredients to manufacturers, said the changes could create demand for smaller portions with higher levels of protein, fibre and other nutrients. It also pointed to opportunities for products with softer textures, balanced flavours and lighter formulations that allow users to participate more comfortably in social eating occasions.“A change in appetite can lead to a broader change in the relationship people have with food,” said Harsch Koshti, regional marketing director for IFF Taste in Greater Asia.The company did not disclose the exact number or demographic profile of participants. The findings therefore offer an early view of GLP-1 users in three large cities rather than a nationwide measure of how Indians taking the medicines eat or shop..Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Nvidia could hit a $13 trillion market cap, analyst says
articles.summary: Talk about an Nvidia bull!
articles.body:
Raymond James analyst Simon Leopold lifted his price target on Nvidia to $550 from $352 in a note on Thursday. Crunching the numbers, Leopold's price target assumes about 130% upside from current levels.

That would estimate Nvidia reaches a $13 trillion market cap. The chipmaker's current market stands at about $5.2 trillion.

"While near-term results were outstanding with sales doubling year over year, it is the FY28 outlook for 70% growth that the investors will applaud," Leopold said. "Architectural Evolutions (LPU:NVL racks at 1:1 and agentic CPU Vera racks) accelerate growth. Capital returns remain robust, with a record $26 billion returned in F2Q27, including $20 billion of buybacks and a $0.25/share quarterly dividend totaling $6 billion."

The average price target on Nvidia is $306, per Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data.

Nvidia stock rose as much as 9% on the results and upbeat outlook.

Indeed, Nvidia's quarter and outlook warranted the strong market response.

Nvidia saw adjusted earnings per share of $2.22 on revenue of $96.2 billion. These were better than the $2.09 per share and revenue of $92.3 billion the Street expected.

Nvidia's Data Center revenue, which includes Hyperscalers and AI Clouds, Industrial, and Enterprise (ACIE), came in at $89 billion versus a projected $85.8 billion.

Edge Computing, which includes Nvidia's other businesses, such as physical AI and gaming, brought in $7.2 billion. Analysts were expecting $6.6 billion.

Nvidia projected fiscal third quarter revenue of between $105.8 billion and $110.1 billion. Wall Street was calling for $105.1 billion.

This would be the first quarter above $100 billion in revenue for Nvidia, Stifel's Roy said.

Nvidia said late Wednesday after reporting its fiscal second quarter earnings that it sees 70% revenue growth for fiscal year 2028. This was above analyst forecasts for 45% growth. The sales gain would be larger if not for memory chip shortages, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said.

"Rubin and LPU ramps are happening faster than our model," Leopold added. "Vera Rubin entered production shipments this month. Purchase orders from every hyperscaler, AI cloud and system OEM, positioning it as Nvidia's fastest ramp ever. Groq 3 LPX is already in full production, with volume shipments later this quarter and neocloud Nebius the first adopter. Vera Rubin chip revenue itself is expected to reach ~20% of Data Center revenue in F3Q27."

articles.title: Dream11 completes shift away from fantasy gaming
articles.summary: India Business News: Dream11 ends fantasy prize contests, rebrands as AI-first global sports engagement platform with content, streaming, stats, communities and fan experiences.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Dream11 has completed its transition away from fantasy sports, dropping all prize-based contests and repositioning itself as a global sports engagement platform, the company said on Thursday.The move marks a sharp break from the business that made Dream11 one of India’s best-known gaming companies. The platform will now focus on sports content, live streaming, scores, statistics, commentary, communities, fan experiences and social contests.The shift comes about a year after India banned online money games under the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, forcing Dream11 and other real-money gaming companies to discontinue paid contests. Rules under the law came into force from May 1 this year.Dream11 had continued experimenting with free-to-play formats after the ban. Its latest move goes further, removing prizes altogether and expanding the platform beyond its core fantasy gaming business.The company said the new Dream11 will be an “AI-first” platform, offering personalised feeds based on the sports, leagues, teams and players followed by users. It also plans to expand across multiple sports and target audiences globally.“With 300 million users, Dream11 understands what a true sports fan really wants—not just the sport, but the community,” CEO Vaibhav Kokal said. The company is building a platform “made in India, for the World”, he added.The transition underlines the extent to which the regulatory reset has reshaped the real-money gaming industry. Fantasy sports companies had built their businesses around users paying to enter contests and competing for cash prizes. That model was effectively shut down after the Centre prohibited online games involving monetary stakes.For Dream11, the challenge now is to convert its vast fantasy sports user base into an audience for content and other forms of sports engagement. Its new offering will range from watching matches and tracking scores to interacting with other fans and booking sports experiences.The move also places Dream11 in a much broader and more competitive market, where it will vie for users’ attention with sports broadcasters, streaming platforms, social media companies and dedicated sports-content apps, rather than primarily competing with other fantasy gaming firms.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Hindalco commissions India’s first superfine PPT ATH plant in Belagavi
articles.summary: India Business News: Hindalco commissions India’s first superfine PPT ATH plant in Belagavi; 30,000 tpa capacity, halogen-free flame retardant, renewable-powered, cuts imports.
articles.body: Belagavi: Hindalco Industries Ltd, the metals flagship of the Aditya Birla Group, has commissioned India’s first greenfield manufacturing facility for superfine precipitated aluminium trihydrate (PPT ATH) in Belagavi. The facility is expected to strengthen the company’s specialty materials portfolio and reduce India’s dependence on imports for critical fire-safety applications.With an annual production capacity of 30,000 tonnes, the plant is a key addition to Hindalco’s specialty alumina business. The company said the facility supports the Centre’s Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative by enabling domestic production of an advanced flame-retardant material.Superfine PPT ATH is a halogen-free flame retardant used in cables, polymer insulators, thermal insulation products, composites and industrial coatings. It helps suppress flame propagation and reduce smoke generation while avoiding the release of toxic halogen-acid gases during combustion.Hindalco said the plant’s phase-I capacity can meet nearly the entire domestic demand from the wire and cable industry. The facility has been designed for phased expansion to 60,000 tonnes a year to cater to future market growth.“The commissioning of our Superfine Precipitated Hydrate plant in Belagavi will further strengthen our leadership position and enhance our high-value specialty alumina portfolio in India,” said Satish Pai, managing director, Hindalco Industries.Saurabh Khedekar, CEO, alumina business, said the company’s InnoSafe solution would support safer and more sustainable infrastructure by improving fire resistance and smoke suppression.Hindalco’s specialty alumina business has a production capacity of around 800,000 tonnes a year and offers more than 120 grades of specialty alumina and alumina hydrates. The addition of superfine PPT ATH expands its presence in advanced flame-retardant applications.Developed through Hindalco’s in-house research and innovation ecosystem, the Belagavi facility features automated manufacturing controls and integrated quality systems. The company said the plant is powered entirely by renewable energy sources, including biomass, solar and wind.Hindalco also said its refinery has achieved a greenhouse-gas intensity of 0.4 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent per tonne of alumina.The facility is expected to strengthen India’s manufacturing capabilities in fire-safe electrical, infrastructure and mobility applications while expanding the domestic availability of advanced specialty materials.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Deepinder Goyal’s Temple acquires London longevity clinic LongeVus
articles.summary: India Business News: Temple, Deepinder Goyal’s wearable startup, acquires London longevity clinic LongeVus, adding founders as CMO and head of science to validate its device.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Deepinder Goyal’s wearable technology startup Temple has acquired London-based longevity medicine practice LongeVus, bringing its founders Robert Mohr and Avi Roy into the company as it builds its clinical and scientific capabilities ahead of a wider product launch.Financial details of the acquisition were not disclosed.Mohr will join Temple as chief medical officer, while Roy will take over as head of science, Goyal said in a post on Thursday. LongeVus will continue to operate as part of Temple, with its founders continuing to serve its existing clients.The acquisition comes as Temple works to validate the science behind its wearable device, which is worn on the temple and is designed to track physiological signals. Goyal said Mohr and Roy had spent the past two months using the device and working with Temple’s scientists to pressure-test its data and the company’s “Entropy” metric.The two subsequently became involved in Temple’s scientific validation efforts.Roy said Temple had spent about two years developing its sensor technology and building the scientific evidence underpinning the product ahead of its launch. The team is now working to get its validation studies through peer review, he said.Temple emerged publicly earlier this year after raising $54 million at a post-money valuation of about $190 million. Its investors include Peak XV Partners, Steadview Capital, Dharana Capital and Info Edge Ventures, along with a group of startup founders and early Zomato investors.In May, Goyal said the first 100 Temple devices were ready to be shipped to selected early users, including athletes, scientists and doctors, who would provide feedback on the product.Goyal stepped down as chief executive of Zomato parent Eternal earlier this year, saying he wanted more time and freedom to pursue higher-risk experiments outside the listed company. He continues to serve as vice chairman of Eternal.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mallya cites Subhash Chandra settlement to renew recovery questions
articles.summary: India Business News: Vijay Mallya cites Subhash Chandra’s insolvency settlement to question India’s bank recoveries, claiming govt figures exceed his adjudicated debt.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Fugitive businessman Vijay Mallya has cited the debt settlement of media baron Subhash Chandra to renew his questions over the amount banks have recovered from him, claiming government figures show recoveries far exceeding his adjudicated debt.In a post on X, Mallya congratulated Chandra after National Company Law Tribunal approved his personal insolvency repayment plan, under which he is to pay Rs 6.5 crore to settle admitted creditor claims of more than Rs 22,000 crore.“If True, many congratulations to my friend Subhash,” Mallya wrote. “Banks and Government have admitted having recovered Rs 14,100 crores from me against a Judgement debt of Rs 6,203 crores. Many more borrowers have settled at a fraction. Indian Debt Resolution Justice I presume. No media questions.”Mallya’s remarks refer to India’s debt resolution framework. While Chandra’s settlement involves a steep haircut for lenders, Mallya has repeatedly questioned why, according to figures cited by the government, recoveries from him have exceeded the amount he says was adjudicated against him.In December last year, Mallya questioned the Centre and public sector banks regarding what he described as conflicting statements on the amounts recovered from him. He demanded an independent investigation into the figures.Mallya had said the finance ministry informed Parliament that Rs 14,100 crore had been recovered from him, while banks had put the recovery figure at about Rs 10,000 crore. He also questioned differing claims about the amount still outstanding.Mallya has argued that the government and lenders should provide a detailed statement accounting for all amounts recovered and credited against his liabilities. articles.title: One in three AI-using firms forgo some software buys: McKinsey
articles.summary: India Business News: McKinsey State of AI 2026: 1 in 3 AI-using firms skipped software buys, building in-house with coding agents; adoption rises, EBIT gains lag, costs constrain.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Nearly one in three respondents at organisations that regularly use artificial intelligence said their companies had decided against buying at least one software product or feature. They built the required functionality in-house using AI coding tools instead, according to McKinsey’s State of AI in 2026 report.The finding points to an emerging shift in how companies allocate technology budgets. AI coding agents can plan and execute multi-step software-development tasks with less human intervention. This is giving companies another option beyond buying packaged software from an external vendor.The trend was strongest in the technology sector. Around 41% of respondents from technology companies said their organisations had forgone at least one software purchase in favour of an internal build. The share was 39% in healthcare, 38% each in professional services and energy and materials, and 36% among financial institutions.“The rise of software coding agents and in-house development is one clear sign of this broader shift,” McKinsey senior partner Lieven Van der Veken said in the report. He added that this did not mean companies would build everything themselves or stop working with technology partners. They were becoming more deliberate about what to buy and what to develop internally.Large companies are moving faster. Among respondents from organisations with at least $1 billion in annual revenue, 31% said software coding agents were being scaled across the enterprise. The corresponding share among smaller organisations was 17%.Overall, 89% of respondents said their organisations regularly used AI in at least one business function. The share reporting that AI was being scaled across the enterprise rose to 44% from 38% a year earlier.However, wider adoption has not yet translated into a similar increase in financial returns. Only 37% said AI had made a positive contribution to their organisations’ earnings before interest and taxes. That was largely unchanged from 2025. In contrast, 80% said AI had improved their individual productivity and half said it helped them make better decisions.Costs are also emerging as a constraint. One in five respondents said AI-related operating expenses, including the cost of processing tokens, had limited its use at their organisations. Yet 60% expected their companies to increase AI investments over the next year.Expectations of job losses have also run ahead of actual changes. Last year, 32% expected AI to reduce their organisation’s workforce. Only 14% now said such a decline had occurred over the past year. However, 39% again expect workforce reductions in the coming year.McKinsey surveyed 1,719 participants across 97 countries between May 4 and June 8. The report did not provide India-specific findings.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
